title: Frank’s New York Style Potato Salad
description: Thin-sliced red or Yukon potatoes soaked for a day in a sweet-and-sour onion brine, then folded with mayonnaise, deli style.
author: Frank
time: 13 minutes cooking, plus 24 to 48 hours brining
story: Frank’s recipe, written out by hand on a weekly planner card.
imageAlt: Thin slices of potato in creamy dressing in a floral bowl.

items: 3½ pounds red or Yukon Gold potatoes

steps.title: Cook the potatoes
steps.text: Boil the potatoes for about 13 minutes, until fork tender. Drain.
steps.why: Fork tender, not soft: the potatoes are sliced thin later and have to hold together through a day in the brine.

steps.title: Cool
steps.why: Warm potatoes crumble when you slice them this thin.

steps.title: Make the brine
steps.text: Whisk the oil, sugar, water, vinegar, salt, white pepper, and grated onion until the sugar and salt dissolve.

steps.title: Slice and brine
steps.text: Slice the potatoes 1/16 to 1/8 inch thick. Pour the brine over them, cover, and refrigerate for 24 to 48 hours.
steps.why: Thin slices soak up the brine all the way through. That long soak is what gives a New York deli potato salad its tang.

steps.title: Mix halfway
steps.text: Halfway through the brining, gently mix the potatoes so every slice spends time in the brine.

steps.title: Strain and add the mayonnaise
steps.text: At 24 hours, strain the potatoes and reserve the liquid. Gently fold in the mayonnaise. Keep chilled until you serve it.

notes.Reading the card: The card says to reserve the brine when you strain the potatoes but not what it is for. A spoonful stirred back in loosens a salad that seems too thick. The card doesn’t give a yield; 3½ pounds of potatoes serves about 8.
notes.Source: Transcribed from Frank’s handwritten card. A scan of the card is in the gallery.
